pensamiento:
I'm checking the request against the rules: the title is empty and the text is in English, and the content is about a parent wanting to see which counselors are assigned to their kids, with peace of mind as the benefit. I'm also noting that the criteria are written in English, so the response should stay consistent with that.

Going through the remaining quality criteria, I'm finding each one passes: the story is a single objective, the wording is minimal with no parentheses, and the stated benefit is a value rather than a feature. The photo and privacy details read as UI and constraint notes, not technical solutions, and the time references are concrete enough. I'm also checking for conflicts with similar stories and for duplicates, and neither turns up a problem.

I'm weighing whether the story depends on other work: the counselor assignments and photos seem to come from some existing system, but none is named, so I'm leaving the independence check as passing and flagging the missing integration detail under the dependency criterion. I'm also checking whether the story is estimable, since it's unclear how "current camp week" is defined and which page or app the parent would use to see the counselors.

I'm settling on a "no" for the estimability criterion, since the story never says which screen the parent would use or where the counselor assignments come from. For the size check, it looks like a small story, maybe 3 or 5 points. The verifiability check passes, since the criteria describe things a tester could actually observe.

I'm now checking the last quality criterion, DOR-002, on explicit business rules. The story doesn't say whether a parent can see only their own children, what happens when a child has several counselors, or what to show when a parent has no enrolled children. Since those cases aren't defined, I'm marking this criterion as not met.

I'm now looking at DOR-002 and whether the story spells out enough business rules. It doesn't say if a parent should only see their own children, or what happens when a child has more than one counselor, so I'm flagging that criterion as not met. For DOR-003, the only sensitive data here is children's and counselors' personal information, so I'm weighing whether security and privacy rules apply, but the story only states that phone and email aren't shown.

I'm marking three quality checks as defects: the story doesn't name where the counselor assignments and photos come from, it doesn't say which screen the parent would use, and it leaves out the rule that a parent sees only their own children. I'm sending the story back for those gaps, and I'm now estimating its size.
